PLAINTIFF’S MOTION UNDER FEDERAL RULE OF CIVIL

PROCEDURE 26(d)(1) FOR LEAVE TO SERVE THREE LIMITED
INTERROGATORIES ON NCMEC BEFORE THE RULE 26(f) CONFERENCE

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine, pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1),
moves for leave to serve three interrogatories on Defendant National Center for Missing &
Exploited Children (““NCMEC”) before the conference required by Federal Rule of Civil
Procedure 26(f). The three interrogatories are set forth in Exhibit A and are reproduced verbatim
here:

INTERROGATORY NO. 1: Excluding information supplied by Plaintiff in the
April 9, 2026 materials, court filings, public sources, and information obtained or
added after original receipt by NCMEC, did either of the two CyberTipline reports
referenced in NCMEC’s April 22, 2026 letters, as originally received by NCMEC,
contain or otherwise identify “Marvelle J. Ballentine”?

INTERROGATORY NO. 2: Subject to the same exclusions, did either report, as
originally received by NCMEC, contain or otherwise identify “Jay Ballentine”?

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document15_ Filed 08/20/26 Page 2 of 5 PagelD# 235

INTERROGATORY NO. 3: Subject to the same exclusions, did either report, as
originally received by NCMEC, contain’ or _ otherwise _ identify
jaychizza@icloud.com?

NCMEC may answer each interrogatory with one of three responses: “Yes,” “No,” or
“Unable to determine after reasonable inquiry.” The interrogatories seek no explanation and no
report content.

NCMEC has placed the two CyberTipline reports at issue in its pending Motion to Dismiss.
ECF No. 10. Its Memorandum in Support (ECF No. 11) argues that the April 22, 2026 statement
was true and that Plaintiff “cannot plausibly assert” falsity “because he does not have access to
those reports.” NCMEC holds the two reports. Plaintiff does not. The three interrogatories ask
NCMEC to state whether each of Plaintiff’s three identifiers appeared in either report as originally
received by NCMEC.

This Motion seeks no other relief. It seeks no production of either report or any portion of
either report; no document, deposition, communication, metadata, report number, submitter
identity, date, or narrative; no discovery from any Defendant other than NCMEC; and no
commencement of general discovery. The grounds for this Motion are set forth in the
accompanying Memorandum in Support. A proposed order and Exhibit A are submitted herewith.

Pursuant to Local Civil Rule 37(E), Plaintiff and counsel for NCMEC conferred by
telephone on August 20, 2026 regarding the three interrogatories set forth in Exhibit A. NCMEC
did not agree to answer the interrogatories. The parties were unable to resolve the discovery matter.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court grant leave under Rule 26(d)
(1) to serve the three interrogatories set forth in Exhibit A on NCMEC before the Rule 26(f)

conference; require NCMEC to answer them under oath, pursuant to Rule 33, within seven
